newsitem.title: USA: US SPR should be able to blunt oil shortage - Pena.
newsitem.headline: US SPR should be able to blunt oil shortage - Pena.

text.p: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve should be maintained to hold enough oil to blunt effects of an oil shortage, Federico Pena, President Clinton's choice for energy secretary, said Thursday.

In his remarks for his confirmation hearing before the Senate Energy Committee, Pena said the nation needs an energy strategy that "maintains our Strategic Petroleum Reserve at levels that respect our international responsibilities in order to blunt the impact of a future oil shortage."
Several sales of SPR oil have been held in the last year to pay to operate the reserve and to raise funds for eduction programs.

Pena also said the energy strategy should expand use of natural gas, diversify oil supply options in areas such as the Western Hemisphere, central Asia and the Caspian Sea, increase domestic energy output, and stress efficiency and development of clean, renewable fuels.

In questioning by Sen. Don Nickles, R-Okla., Pena said one of the toughest challenges will be keeping marginal wells going. "I don't have the answer today on how we will address it, but it will be a priority," he said.
